stage: bare-metal NR image for the compiled Qwen3 graph (1 layer)
what_this_proves: the compiled graph, with its operators replaced by calls into the Triton static library, links into a bare-metal NR image that passes the full FPGA instruction audit
not_yet: it has NOT been uploaded or run on the board

graph.descriptor_order: 14 parameters in compiled layout order, then ids, cache position, K cache, V cache
graph.abi_derived_from: the lowered module, not hand-written; an earlier hand-written prototype had the wrong arity

parameter_segment.note: this is the FP32 buffer the compiled graph actually reads; W8A8 (validation/weight-image.json) is the deployment target once the graph is quantised

build_fixes_along_the_way: the graph's LLVM IR must go through ame_to_word.py and restrict_fpga_assembly.py like the operator pipeline; compiling llc straight to an object skips the fences and the ELF audit rejects it
the model's workspace arrays need explicit `.section .workspace,"aw",@nobits` asm; a plain section attribute emits SHT_PROGBITS and the linker refuses
support.c's 640 MiB operator arena must not be linked: it would collide with the model's own workspace and overflow HIGH
the link must be driven with ld.lld -m elf64lriscv; through clang it picks the host ld, which has no riscv emulation
nr_copy.S needs -march=rv64gcv_zicbom while the rest of the runtime uses rv64gc_zicbom, exactly as common.mk specifies
no -lm: the NR runtime already provides expf/logf/sinf/cosf/sqrtf/powf (nr_math.c) and memrefCopy (nr_runtime.c)

runtime_heap_note.finding: the NR runtime already provides malloc (a bump allocator over __heap_start..__heap_end) and free (a no-op), so the graph's heap use is not a link blocker
runtime_heap_note.budget: 1-layer prefill allocates 13.0 MiB; the whole LOW remainder is available to the bump allocator
runtime_heap_note.caveat: free is a no-op, so allocations accumulate across graph calls; 8 decode steps at 8.3 MiB each is fine, a 28-layer session would not fit without a static memory plan
